extracted.intended_audience: students, teachers, researchers, and aspiring/performance poets seeking an overview of slam poetry
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative norms for composing and performing slam/ spoken-word poetry, and how works are judged in poetry slam competitions. Covers stylistic, performative, and procedural expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral delivery / performance orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: Slam poetry is a dynamic and performance-oriented form that prioritizes oral delivery and the interrelationship between poet, poem, and audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize delivery and stage presence; the form relies heavily on oral performance rather than solely on printed/formal poetic features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional impact / resonance
rubrics_metrics.description: Enthusiasts generally place more importance on the emotional impact of a piece than its formal characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose pieces to generate strong emotional responses; draw on intimate, emotionally charged episodes to communicate impact and universal aspects of experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessible, straightforward language
rubrics_metrics.description: Poets tend to use simple, straightforward language to communicate emotionally impactful, relevant messages that resonate with everyday listeners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overly obscure diction; aim for clarity and directness so diverse audiences can connect with the poem's message.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical relevance and social/political themes
rubrics_metrics.description: Common themes include current events, predominant social issues, and problems arising from cultural, economic, gender, and racial discrimination or injustice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address relevant social themes or personal experiences that illuminate broader social concerns; activism and community-focused content are central to the genre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhythm and musical quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Poets often strive for rhythmic structures that can lend an almost musical quality when performed orally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work on pacing, cadence, and rhythmic devices to enhance musicality in performance even if strict meter is not used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhyme usage (optional and strategic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rhyme schemes are left to the complete discretion of the poet and can be used regularly, irregularly, or not at all; rhymes are generally reserved for particularly powerful passages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use rhyme selectively to heighten emphasis or a climactic moment rather than as a compulsory formal constraint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom from formal structural constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Slam poetry embraces free-form styles that do not necessarily adhere to traditional poetic structural features like rhyme and meter; there are few formal composition rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feel free to experiment with form and structure; the absence of formal constraints shifts evaluation toward performance and content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience engagement and interactivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry slams foster an interactive atmosphere; audiences are encouraged to be responsive and their reactions are part of the event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design performances to invite audience engagement (applause, audible reaction) but balance interactivity so it supports rather than undermines the piece.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judges consider audience reaction and stylistic qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges (often randomly selected audience members) typically consider the audience’s reaction to a piece in addition to its stylistic qualities when assigning scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful pieces typically combine effective stylistic craft with an ability to move or energize the live audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring system (one-to-ten scale) and competitive rounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry slam judges assign scores to individual performances on a one-to-ten scale; competitions typically involve successive rounds with advancement based on scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of the numeric scoring and elimination rounds when crafting length, pacing, and crowd-pleasing moments to maximize scores across rounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain performer rhythm and timing (avoid audience interference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Audiences are encouraged to respond without overtly interfering with the performer’s rhythm or timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manage tempo and space in performance so audience reactions enhance rather than disrupt delivery; avoid cues that invite timing-breaking interruptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composed vs improvised perception ('spoken word' vs 'slam')
rubrics_metrics.description: Some prefer the term 'spoken word' to distance carefully composed works from impressions of improvised or aimless bombast associated with 'slam poetry.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how composition quality and perceived craftsmanship affect reception and legitimacy; carefully composed work can gain critical as well as popular recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event formats: team and individual competitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Major events include team-based National Poetry Slam and the Individual World Poetry Slam; formats (team vs individual) influence performance strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt material and staging based on whether performing solo or as part of a team (e.g., team order, thematic cohesion for team sets).
